Moments of the Noncentral F Distribution

Source: R/moments_nc_F.R
moments_nc_F.Rd

Returns the mean, variance, standard deviation, skewness, and excess kurtosis of a noncentral F distribution with df_1 numerator and df_2 denominator degrees of freedom and noncentrality parameter ncp, in one table. A moment that does not exist for the given df_2 is returned as NA.

Usage

moments_nc_F(df_1, df_2, ncp = 0)

Arguments

df_1

Numerator degrees of freedom, a single positive number.

df_2

Denominator degrees of freedom, a single positive number.

ncp

Noncentrality parameter \(\lambda\), a single non-negative number. Defaults to 0, the central F.

Value

A data.frame (class dmar_tbl) in term / value layout with the mean, variance, sd, skewness, and excess_kurtosis (any of which may be NA when df_2 is too small), followed by the df_1, df_2, and ncp that produced them.

Details

The noncentral F is the reference distribution of the F statistic when an effect is present, so its moments describe the sampling behavior of \(R^2\), eta squared, and the omnibus F test under the alternative. A central F (ncp = 0) is the special case.

The distribution. The noncentral F is \(F = (X_1/\nu_1)/(X_2/\nu_2)\) with \(X_1 \sim \chi^2_{\nu_1}(\lambda)\) a noncentral chi square and \(X_2 \sim \chi^2_{\nu_2}\) independent of it. Its raw moments are $$\mathrm{E}[F^k] = \Bigl(\tfrac{\nu_2}{\nu_1}\Bigr)^k \mathrm{E}[X_1^k]\, \prod_{i=1}^{k}\frac{1}{\nu_2 - 2i}, \qquad \nu_2 > 2k,$$ where the noncentral chi square moments \(\mathrm{E}[X_1^k]\) follow from its cumulants \(\kappa_j = 2^{j-1}(j-1)!\,(\nu_1 + j\lambda)\) (Johnson, Kotz, & Balakrishnan, 1995).

What is returned. The mean is \(\nu_2(\nu_1 + \lambda)/[\nu_1(\nu_2 - 2)]\) and the variance is \(2(\nu_2/\nu_1)^2[(\nu_1 + \lambda)^2 + (\nu_1 + 2\lambda)(\nu_2 - 2)] / [(\nu_2 - 2)^2(\nu_2 - 4)]\). The skewness is the third central moment over the variance to the power 3/2, and the excess kurtosis is the fourth central moment over the squared variance, minus 3 (so that a normal distribution has 0). The mean exists for \(\nu_2 > 2\), the variance for \(\nu_2 > 4\), the skewness for \(\nu_2 > 6\), and the excess kurtosis for \(\nu_2 > 8\); a moment whose condition is not met is returned as NA, and so is the standard deviation when the variance is.

How the moments are computed. A central moment formed as a difference of raw moments loses digits when the degrees of freedom are large, because the raw moments agree in their leading digits: for \(\nu_1 = \nu_2 = 10^6\) and \(\lambda = 0\) that form gives an excess kurtosis of \(-5.29 \times 10^{-5}\), where the value is \(6.60006 \times 10^{-5}\). The function therefore works with the two independent factors of \(F\). Write \(F = (\nu_2/\nu_1) X Y\) with \(X = X_1\) and \(Y = 1/X_2\), and let \(U = X/\mathrm{E}[X] - 1\) and \(V = Y/\mathrm{E}[Y] - 1\), so that \(F/\mathrm{E}[F] - 1 = U + V + UV\) with \(U\) and \(V\) independent and of mean 0. The central moments of \(F/\mathrm{E}[F]\) are then sums of products of the central moments of \(U\) and \(V\), in which every term is nonnegative and nothing cancels. With \(n = \nu_2\), $$u_2 = \kappa_2/\kappa_1^2, \quad u_3 = \kappa_3/\kappa_1^3, \quad c_u = \kappa_4/\kappa_1^4, \quad u_4 = c_u + 3u_2^2,$$ $$v_2 = \frac{2}{n - 4}, \quad v_3 = \frac{16}{(n - 4)(n - 6)}, \quad c_v = \frac{48(5n - 22)}{(n - 4)^2(n - 6)(n - 8)}, \quad v_4 = c_v + 3v_2^2,$$ the second and third central moments and the fourth cumulant of \(U\) and of \(V\) (those of \(V\) from \(\mathrm{E}[Y^k] = \prod_{i=1}^{k} 1/(n - 2i)\)). Then $$m_2 = u_2 + v_2 + u_2 v_2, \qquad \mathrm{Var}(F) = \mathrm{E}[F]^2\, m_2,$$ $$m_3 = u_3 + v_3 + u_3 v_3 + 3u_3 v_2 + 3u_2 v_3 + 6u_2 v_2, \qquad \mathrm{skewness} = m_3 / m_2^{3/2},$$ and the excess kurtosis is \(e_4 / m_2^2\), where $$e_4 = c_u + c_v + c_u c_v + 3c_u v_2^2 + 3u_2^2 c_v + 6u_2^2 v_2^2 + 4u_4 v_3 + 4u_3 v_4 + 6c_u v_2 + 12u_2^2 v_2 + 6u_2 c_v + 12u_2 v_2^2 + 12u_3 v_2 + 12u_2 v_3 + 12u_3 v_3$$ is the fourth central moment of \(U + V + UV\) minus \(3m_2^2\), with the terms that cancel removed algebraically. These expressions are the same quantities as the differences of raw moments above, derived for DMAR; they are not taken from the reference. Checked against exact rational arithmetic in 14 cases with degrees of freedom up to \(10^{12}\) and noncentrality up to \(10^6\), the four moments are right to a relative error of \(5 \times 10^{-16}\). At ordinary degrees of freedom (200 or fewer) the values agree with those of the difference of raw moments to a relative difference of \(10^{-11}\).

References

Johnson, N. L., Kotz, S., & Balakrishnan, N. (1995). Continuous univariate distributions (Vol. 2, 2nd ed., Chapter 30). Wiley.

See also

moments_nc_t for the noncentral t; ci_nc_F for the noncentral F confidence limits used in effect size intervals; df for the density.

Other noncentral distribution moments: moments_nc_chisq(), moments_nc_t()

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

# A noncentral F with 3 and 40 df and noncentrality 8.
moments_nc_F(df_1 = 3, df_2 = 40, ncp = 8)
#>  term            value
#>  mean            3.860
#>  variance        5.766
#>  sd              2.401
#>  skewness        1.335
#>  excess_kurtosis 3.121
#>  df_1            3    
#>  df_2            40   
#>  ncp             8.000

# ncp = 0 is the central F: mean df_2 / (df_2 - 2).
moments_nc_F(df_1 = 3, df_2 = 40)
#>  term            value
#>  mean            1.053
#>  variance        0.841
#>  sd              0.917
#>  skewness        1.980
#>  excess_kurtosis 6.625
#>  df_1            3    
#>  df_2            40   
#>  ncp             0.000

# The variance is undefined for four or fewer denominator df.
moments_nc_F(df_1 = 2, df_2 = 4, ncp = 5)
#>  term            value
#>  mean            7.000
#>  variance        <NA> 
#>  sd              <NA> 
#>  skewness        <NA> 
#>  excess_kurtosis <NA> 
#>  df_1            2    
#>  df_2            4    
#>  ncp             5.000
